  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F000"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [
          "F002",
          "F003",
          "F004"
        ],
        "choice_quote": "F001:F004",
        "choice_text": "An employee of a covered employer who meets all three criteria: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; and (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F001:F004",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.801",
          "§ 825.105(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F001:F002"
        ],
        "scope_text": "For an employee satisfying the requirement of having been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F006:F009"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the applicable break-in-service rules are satisfied."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F005",
          "F007:F009"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (b)(2)"
        ],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F005"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months when there is a break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [
          "F008",
          "F009"
        ],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Either: (i) the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": [
          "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."
        ],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F007"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Where an employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, 38 U.S.C. 4301 et seq.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F008",
        "references": [
          "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."
        ],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F001:F002"
        ],
        "scope_text": "For purposes of determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; for intermittent, occasional, or casual employment, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "Nothing in this section prevents",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Employers are permitted to consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F003"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (c)(2)",
          "§ 825.801",
          "29 CFR part 785"
        ],
        "statement": "Whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work, based on the number of hours worked within the meaning of the FLSA, and is not limited by methods of recordkeeping or inaccurate compensation agreements."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "In determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.801(c)"
        ],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, adding those hours to actual hours worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during a period of absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "can generally",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.801(c)"
        ],
        "statement": "The employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": [
          "29 CFR part 541",
          "§ 825.102",
          "§ 825.801(d)"
        ],
        "statement": "If an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including FLSA-exempt employees, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F014"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer claims that an employee (such as a full-time teacher) is not eligible for FMLA leave when accurate records of hours worked are not maintained.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.102",
          "§ 825.801(d)"
        ],
        "statement": "An employer must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee (for example, full-time teachers of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment) did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "For determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed for a total of at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.300(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time they meet the 12-month eligibility requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.300(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave."
      }
    }
  ]
}

unit_attributes.choice_text: An employee of a covered employer who meets all three criteria: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; and (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For an employee satisfying the requirement of having been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the applicable break-in-service rules are satisfied.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months when there is a break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either: (i) the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Where an employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, 38 U.S.C. 4301 et seq.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; for intermittent, occasional, or casual employment, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Employers are permitted to consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work, based on the number of hours worked within the meaning of the FLSA, and is not limited by methods of recordkeeping or inaccurate compensation agreements.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, adding those hours to actual hours worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during a period of absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including FLSA-exempt employees, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer claims that an employee (such as a full-time teacher) is not eligible for FMLA leave when accurate records of hours worked are not maintained.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee (for example, full-time teachers of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment) did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed for a total of at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time they meet the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.
